newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan c/a surplus declining, but tempo to slow-MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan c/a surplus declining, but tempo to slow-MOF.

text.p: Japan's current account surplus is on a declining trend, but the tempo of the decline will slow down, a Finance Ministry official told a news conference on Thursday.
"Although the shrinking trend of the current account surplus remains unchanged, the tempo (of the fall) will slow down," the official said.

He said looking at the recent movements, the deficit in services continued to rise, but added that the increase in the income surplus, along with the slowing of the declining trend in the trade surplus, will slow down the tempo of the shrinkage in the current account surplus.
The ministry announced earlier that Japan's surplus in its current account rose sharply in January, marking the first increase in 17 months.

The surplus totalled 150.7 billion yen in January, compared with a surplus of 32.6 billion yen a year earlier. But the surplus in merchandise trade alone fell to 229.3 billion yen from 271.3 billion yen a year earlier.
Meanwhile, the surplus in income stood at 518.8 billion yen in January, the highest for the month of January in 12 years, the ministry said.
The deficit in services shrank a bit to 513.7 billion yen in January from a 581.2 billion yen deficit a year ago due to an increase in Japanese firms' profits from commodities dealings.
But the deficit in travel, a component of the services account, posted a deficit of 305.6 billion yen, the largest for the month of January in six years.
